rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels' intercession has no effect until God permits it, and He permits them to intercede for believers in whom He is pleased.
rows.anchor: إلا من بعد أن يأذن الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says angels intercede only for those whom God approves, as 21:28 also states.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد لا تشفع الملائكة إلا لمن رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny the afterlife call angels female because they claim the angels are God's daughters, though they have no certain knowledge of this.
rows.anchor: حين زعموا أنهم بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here truth means knowledge: conjecture neither supplies knowledge nor takes its place.
rows.anchor: الحق هنا معناه العلم أي الظن لا يغني عن العلم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to turn from those who abandon God's remembrance and seek only worldly life, bear with them, and continue calling them to truth.
rows.anchor: لا تقابلهم على أفعالهم واحتملهم ولا تدع مع هذا وعظمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their knowledge stops at neglecting reflection on the afterlife and pursuing immediate pleasure; this low, animal-like aim is unworthy of a rational person.
rows.anchor: منتهى علمهم وهو مبلغ خسيس لا يرضى به لنفسه عاقل

words: إن ربك هو أعلم بمن ضل عن سبيله وهو أعلم بمن اهتدى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows best who strays and who is guided, and will requite each according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: فيجازي كلا منهم على حسب أعمالهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ defines lَمَم as a deed done once in a while without becoming a habit; Umayya's line uses ألما for such a lapse.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء اللمم أن يفعل الإنسان الشيء في الحين

rows.speaker: أمية
rows.claim: Umayya's line uses ألما as evidence for the occasional, nonhabitual sense of lَمَم.
rows.anchor: قال أمية: إن تغفر اللهم تغفر جما وأي عبد لك لا ألما

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet recited the two lines and explained them as meaning that he had not committed a sin.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أن إلنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ينشدهما

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's cited line uses ألم in the sense of briefly encountering or partaking of something.
rows.anchor: وقال أعشى باهله: تكفيه حزة فلذ إن ألم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajnna is the plural of janīn, an embryo; Ruʾba's line pictures embryos hidden in throats.
rows.anchor: أجنة جمع جنين قال رؤبة: أجنة في مستكنات الحلق

rows.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
rows.claim: The poet uses janīn for a person hidden in a grave, attesting its sense of something concealed.
rows.anchor: وقال عمرو بن كلثوم: ولا شمطاء لم يترك شقاها لها من تسعة إلا جنينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akdā means to cut off a gift, likened to a well stopping at hard bedrock; the root also describes exhausted fingers, thickened nails, and poor plant yield.
rows.anchor: وأكدى أي قطع العطاء كما تقطع البئر الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-lamam is accusative as an exception from sins and indecencies; it is lesser than these yet still belongs to their category.
rows.anchor: إلا اللمم منصوب على الاستثناء من الإثم والفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time clause may be governed by aʿlamu bikum, attached to ajinna as its description, or understood with an omitted clause describing the embryos.
rows.anchor: إذ أنشأكم العامل في إذ قوله أعلم بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is understood as annahu lā taziru and substitutes for the preceding reference to what is in Moses' pages; mā is a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى تقديره أنه لا تزر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي وجماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: They report the passage about ʿUthmān: after his foster brother ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ promised to bear his sins if he stopped donating, ʿUthmān gave him a camel and ceased giving; it says he left his post at Uḥud, then resumed his former practice.
rows.anchor: فعاد عثمان إلى ما كان عليه عن ابن عباس والسدي والكلبي وجماعة من المفسرين

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Zayd say the verses concern al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who returned to shirk after a critic pledged to carry his punishment, paid the man only part of the promised amount, then withheld the rest.
rows.anchor: فنزلت أفرأيت الذي تولى عن الإيمان وأعطى صاحبه الضامن قليلا وأكدى

words: هو أعلم بكم إذ أنشأكم من الأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew people before creating them; their creation from earth first refers to their father Adam, made from the earth's surface.
rows.anchor: أي أنشأ أباكم آدم من أديم الأرض

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhī takes the earth reference to all people: God creates them from foods derived from earth, using His customary creation through their combined substances.
rows.anchor: قال البلخي يجوز أن يكون المراد به جميع الخلق

words: وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم
rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God knew, while they were embryos, what each person would do and what their eventual end would be.
rows.anchor: أي علم من كل نفس ما هي صانعة وإلى ما هي صائرة عن الحسن

words: وإذ أنتم أجنة في بطون أمهاتكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage may also mean that God knew people's weakness and inclination toward minor lapses in the womb, so He certainly knows their deeds after they exist.
rows.anchor: علم ضعفكم وميل طباعكم إلى اللمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not exalt yourselves or praise yourselves for qualities you do not possess, since God knows you better.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعظموها ولا تمدحوها بما ليس لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is not to claim purity for one's good deeds, which would hinder devotion and humility and encourage ostentation.
rows.anchor: لا تزكوها بما فيها من الخير ليكون أقرب إلى النسك والخشوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the pious is those who avoid polytheism and major sins.
rows.anchor: أي اتقى الشرك والكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is those who act righteously, obey, and sincerely devote their deeds.
rows.anchor: هو اعلم بمن بر وأطاع وأخلص العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person turned away from the truth.
rows.anchor: أي أدبر عن الحق

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains akdā as holding back the gift and cutting it off.
rows.anchor: أي أمسك عن العطية وقطع عن الفراء

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains akdā as refusing very firmly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: منع منعا شديدا عن المبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen matter at issue is the punishment: does the miser know and see that another person will bear his punishment for him?
rows.anchor: أي ما غاب عنه من أمر العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference is to the books of the Torah and the pages of Abraham; waffā means Abraham completed and fulfilled what he was commanded.
rows.anchor: أي بل ألم يخبر ولم يحدث بما في أسفار التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say Abraham conveyed the message to his people, or completed everything God required and tested him with.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بلغ قومه وأدى ما أمر به إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul carries another soul's burden, meaning no one is punished for another person's sin.
rows.anchor: أي لا تحمل نفس حاملة حمل أخرى والمعنى لا تؤخذ نفس بإثم غيرها

words: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause is joined to the preceding teaching and also belongs to the pages of Moses and Abraham: a person earns only the reward for their own work, not another's.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله ألا تزر وهذا أيضا ما في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If someone calls another to faith and the person responds, the caller is praised derivatively because the caller's own effort caused it; without one's own work there is no earned reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: ومتى دعا غيره إلى الإيمان فأجابه إليه فهو محمود على ذلك

words: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In al-Wālibī's transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās says this ruling was abrogated in Islamic law because 52:21 raises descendants' rank although they did not earn it through their own deeds.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في رواية الوالبي قال إن هذا منسوخ الحكم في شريعتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The linked verse says God raises the descendants in rank although they did not earn it by their deeds; Ibn Abbas cites it as evidence that the prior ruling was abrogated.
rows.anchor: رفع درجة الذرية وإن لم يستحقوها بأعمالهم

words: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى
rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima similarly confines the rule to the communities of Abraham and Moses; this community can benefit from others' efforts performed on its behalf.
rows.anchor: نحو هذا قال عكرمة إن ذلك لقوم إبراهيم وموسى فأما هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the view that the ruling remains, the verse bars deputation in acts of worship except where evidence permits it, such as pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: ومن قال إنه غير منسوخ الحكم قال الآية تدل على منع النيابة في الطاعات

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A woman said her father had not performed pilgrimage, and the Prophet told her to perform it for him.
rows.anchor: أن امرأة قالت يا رسول الله أن أبي لم يحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's deeds and efforts will later be seen, meaning the person will be recompensed for them.
rows.anchor: يعني أن ما يفعله الإنسان ويسعى فيه لا بد أن يرى فيما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then the effort itself is repaid in full: lasting reward for obedience, with the pronoun referring to the effort; on Judgment Day the servant sees it and receives its fullest recompense.
rows.anchor: والهاء في يجزاه عائدة إلى السعي والمعنى أنه يرى العبد سعيه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة غير سهل
rows.claim: Medina and Basra readers other than Sahl assimilate the form and omit tanwīn and hamza; Qālūn from Nāfiʿ instead reports a hamzated, silent form.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة غير سهل عاد لولى مدغمة

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers pronounce ʿĀdan al-ūlā with tanwīn and a clear hamza, without assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون عادا الأولى منونة مهموزة غير مدغمة

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة ويعقوب
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and Yaʿqūb read Thamūd without tanwīn; the other readers use tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة ويعقوب وثمود فما أبقى بغير تنوين

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abū ʿUthmān criticizes Abū ʿAmr's assimilation because the article's lām receives only the temporary vowel of the hamza, not a stable vowel.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان أساء عندي أبو عمرو في قراءته لأنه أدغم النون في لام المعرفة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan reports Arabs saying hal-ḥamr and dropping the wasl alif because the lām is vowelled, supporting the permissibility of assimilation.
rows.anchor: ولكن كان أبو الحسن روى عن بعض العرب أنه كان يقول هذا لحمر قد جاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With a clear hamza and tanwīn, the article's lām is silent, so the two vowelless sounds meet and tanwīn takes kasra; analogous assimilations can omit tanwīn, though this is not the transmitted reading here.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي القول في عادا الأولى أن من حقق الهمزة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects the charge that Abū ʿAmr erred: lightening the hamza can free the lām from its silent status, or assimilation can be allowed by analogy with consonants that are otherwise silent.
rows.anchor: وخرج عن الإساءة التي نسبها إليه أبو عثمان من وجهين

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ's hamzated form is explained by analogy with Ibn Kathīr's ʿalā suʾqihi: proximity of the ḍamma makes the wāw seem to bear it, a reported but uncommon dialect.
rows.anchor: وأما ما روي عن نافع من أنه همز فقال عاد لؤلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ultimate end is with the Lord: the final destination is His reward and punishment, where action comes to an end.
rows.anchor: يعني وأن إلى ثواب ربك وعقابه آخر الأمر والمنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source defines manā as determination; the cited verse uses it for what the determiner ordains, and maniyya is named for being determined.
rows.anchor: المني التقدير يقال منى يمني فهو مان

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited line uses manā for what is apportioned or ordained.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: حتى تبين ما يمني لك الماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nashʾa means fashioned, created origination, contrasted with mere willing.
rows.anchor: والنشأة الصنعة المخترعة خلاف المشيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqnā derives from qinya, lasting principal property kept for oneself; iqtināʾ is keeping something permanently, and qanāh is connected because it is retained.
rows.anchor: وأقنى من القنية وهي أصل المال وما يقتنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shiʿrā is the star behind Gemini, one of the two stars in the Lion's forearm, and was worshiped in pre-Islamic times.
rows.anchor: والشعرى النجم الذي خلف الجوزاء وهو أحد كوكبي ذراع الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muʾtafikah is a city overturned so its top became bottom; ifk is falsehood because it reverses meaning from its proper direction.
rows.anchor: والمؤتفكة المنقلبة وهي التي صار أعلاها أسفلها وأسفلها أعلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahawehā means cast down through the air; the verb is also used of a hand reaching down, but not of descending stairs.
rows.anchor: وأهوى أي أنزل بها في الهواء ومنه أهوى بيده ليأخذ كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azifat al-āzifah means the approaching event has drawn near; al-Nābigha's verse attests the usage.
rows.anchor: وأزفت الأرزفة أي دنت الدانية قال النابغة

rows.speaker: كعب بن زهير
rows.claim: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr's line uses azafā for approaching or drawing near.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب بن زهير: بان الشباب وأمسى الشيب قد أزفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sumūd means amusement and sām id means heedless or distracted; the cited line uses the root for idly passing time.
rows.anchor: والسمود اللهو والسامد اللاهي يقال سمد يسمد

rows.speaker: عطاء والجبائي
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and al-Jubbāʾī understand God as causing laughter and weeping through joy and grief, as one says that someone made him laugh or cry.
rows.anchor: أي فعل سبب الضحك والبكاء من السرور والحزن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says God makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise and the people of Hell weep in Hell.
rows.anchor: أضحك أهل الجنة في الجنة وأبكى أهل النار في النار عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laughter and crying may be human acts: 9:82 attributes them to people, as does 53:60.
rows.anchor: والضحك والبكاء من فعل الإنسان قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God creates laughter and crying; laughter opens the face's features from joy and wonder in the heart, while crying is tears from grief or a tender heart, sometimes mixed with joyful memory.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن إن الله سبحانه هو الخالق للضحك والبكاء والضحك تفتح أسرار الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say God makes trees laugh with blossoms and clouds cry with rain, or gives the obedient mercy and the disobedient punishment.
rows.anchor: أضحك الأشجار بالأنوار وأبكى السحاب بالأمطار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone creates death and life: whoever could cause death could cause its opposite, but no one can give life except God; He raises the dead for recompense.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر على ذلك غيره لأنه لو قدر على الموت لقدر على الحياة

rows.speaker: عطاء والضحاك والجبائي
rows.claim: They explain the two sexes as every animal's male and female, formed from male and female fluid when it is emitted and deposited in the womb.
rows.anchor: والنطفة ماء الرجل والمرأة التي يخلق منها الولد عن عطاء والضحاك والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives tamnā from estimation: the fluid is placed in the woman's womb according to a determined measure.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تمنى أن تقدر وهو أصله فالمعنى تلقى على تقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second creation is resurrection for recompense. Although ʿalā sounds like an obligation, God's promise of reward and compensation for earthly suffering entails a further life for judgment and justice, and He must fulfill His promise.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم يعوض في الدنيا وخلى بين المظلوم والظالم فلا بد من دار أخرى

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ explains that God enriches people with wealth and grants them lasting property and principal wealth beyond what they need.
rows.anchor: أي أغنى الناس بالأموال وإعطاء القنية وأصول المال

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujāhid, and Qatāda explain aqnā as giving servants.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أقنى أي أخدم عن الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains aghnā as making rich and aqnā as making content with what one is given.
rows.anchor: أغنى مول وأقنى أرضى بما أعطى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd offers the contrasting explanation that God impoverishes and deprives whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: وأقنى أي أفقر وحرم من شاء عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the creator, originator, and owner of Sirius, so people must not make a created, owned thing their god.
rows.anchor: أي فلا تتخذوا المربوب المملوك إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source says Khuzāʿa worshiped Sirius, first worshiped by Abū Kabsha, a maternal ancestor of the Prophet; Quraysh called the Prophet Ibn Abī Kabsha because he differed from their religion.
rows.anchor: إن خزاعة كانت تعبدها وأول من عبدها أبو كبشة أحد أجداد النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ʿĀd are the people of Hūd, destroyed by a violent, freezing wind; their surviving descendants were called the later ʿĀd.
rows.anchor: وهو عاد بن إرم وهم قوم هود أهلكهم الله بريح صرصر عاتية

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says they perished through one another's oppression and killed one another until they were wiped out.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق أهلكوا ببغي بعضهم على بعض فتفانوا بالقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also destroyed Thamūd; mā is fronted and therefore cannot make what follows an object of abqā.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون منصوبا بأبقى

words: وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses opened with anna are all treated as teachings in the pages of Abraham and Moses, following the report of what those pages contain.
rows.anchor: وإنما فتحت أن في هذه المواضع كلها لأن جميعها في صحف إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the moon split into two parts during the Prophet's time, and the Prophet told those present to bear witness.
rows.anchor: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شقتين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd also swears that he saw Mount Ḥirāʾ between the two halves of the moon.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا عن ابن مسعود أنه قال والذي نفسي بيده لقد رأيت حراء

rows.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
rows.claim: Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim says the moon split into two parts above two mountains; when some said Muḥammad had bewitched them, another replied that he could not have bewitched everyone.
rows.anchor: وعن جبير بن مطعم قال: انشق القمر على عهد رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Companions transmitted the splitting, and the commentators affirm it; the author rejects the future-tense interpretation attributed to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ from his father and to al-Hasan, also rejected by al-Balkhī.
rows.anchor: وقد روى حديث انشقاق القمر جماعة كثيرة من الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the objection that such an event could not have gone unnoticed fails: clouds could conceal it, it happened at night when people might sleep, and not everyone watches the sky.
rows.anchor: لأنه يجوز أن يكون الله تعالى قد حجبه عن أكثرهم بغيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon's splitting is a sign of the Prophet's mission, and his mission and era are among the signs that the Hour is approaching.
rows.anchor: لأن انشقاقه من علامة نبوة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الضحاك وأبو العالية وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Abū al-ʿĀliya, and Qatāda take mustamirr to mean powerful, severe magic that overcomes other magic, from the image of a tightly twisted rope.
rows.anchor: أي قوي شديد يعلو كل سحر عن الضحاك وأبي العالية وقتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid instead takes mustamirr as passing away or vanishing, deriving it from passage.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه سحر ذاهب مضمحل لا يبقى عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say that after the moon split, Quraysh called it magic, prompting the statement that whenever they see a sign they turn away from belief in it.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون لما انشق القمر قال مشركو قريش سحرنا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes Quraysh's obstinate, envious rejection: they turn from examining a miraculous sign and accepting its truth.
rows.anchor: هذا إخبار من الله تعالى عن عناد كفار قريش

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the wording as evidence that the splitting occurred; a miracle is needed to prove prophethood while people can choose, not when they are compelled to know.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وفي هذا دلالة على أن ذلك قد كان ووقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's report that people called it magic shows the event occurred before compulsion to believe, since at that stage they would not label a miracle magic.
rows.anchor: وفي وقت الإلجاء لا يقولون للمعجز أنه سحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied the sign they saw and followed their desires and the falsehood Satan made attractive to them.
rows.anchor: في التكذيب وما زين لهم الشيطان من الباطل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says good settles with good people and evil with evil people; every good or evil deed remains until its doer is recompensed in Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: فالخير يستقر بأهل الخير والشر يستقر بأهل الشر عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says each matter has a reality that will become clear: worldly matters in this life and afterlife matters in the next.
rows.anchor: لكل أمر حقيقة ما كان منه في الدنيا فسيظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an brings weighty reports about earlier disbelieving nations and their destruction as a warning and deterrent from disbelief and denying messengers.
rows.anchor: يعني الأخبار العظيمة في القرآن بكفر من تقدم من الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muzdajar means a lesson or deterrent, literally a verbal noun of restraining oneself.
rows.anchor: أي متعظ وهو بمعنى المصدر أي وازدجار عن الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is complete wisdom that has reached its utmost limit.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن حكمة تامة قد بلغت الغاية والنهاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warnings can avail these people nothing while they deny and turn away.
rows.anchor: أي أي شيء تنفع النذر مع تكذيب هؤلاء وإعراضهم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads both ḥabb and rayḥān in the accusative, with ḥabb coordinated to an implied verb of creation.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر والحب ذا العصف والريحان بالنصب فيهما جميعا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read ḥabb in the nominative and rayḥān in the genitive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف والحب ذو العصف بالرفع والريحان بالجر

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers use the nominative for both nouns; Abū al-Sammāk has a noncanonical nominative reading of wa-l-samāʾ rafaʿahā.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالرفع في الجميع وفي الشواذ قراءة أبي السماك

rows.speaker: بلال بن أبي بردة
rows.claim: Bilāl ibn Abī Burda reads the verb with fatḥa on tāʾ and sīn, or kasra on sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بلال بن أبي بردة ولا تخسروا بفتح التاء والسين

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines ʿaṣf as crop material cut or winnowed and eaten; ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada's line supports the word ʿaṣīfa.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة العصف الذي يعصف فيؤكل من الزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rayḥān can mean edible grain or provision, as in the phrase “Your provision”; al-Namir ibn Taghlib's line is cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: والريحان الحب الذي يؤكل يقال سبحانك وريحانك أي ورزقك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says ʿaṣf means chaff, or the leaves of the crop.
rows.anchor: وقيل العصف والعصيفة ورق الزرع وعن قتادة العصف التبن

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The accusative reading coordinates both nouns with an understood “He created,” supported by 20:53's description of varied plants brought forth from water.
rows.anchor: حمله على وخلق الحب وخلق الريحان وهو الرزق

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With rayḥān nominative, the implied syntax lists fruit, rayḥān, and grain; with it genitive, grain is described as having both husk and provision.
rows.anchor: ومن رفع الريحان فالتقدير فيها فاكهة والريحان والحب ذو العصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source favors edible provision rather than fragrant herbs here, since the passage concerns food for people and livestock; grain freed of its husks is broadly beneficial.
rows.anchor: ويبعد أن يكون الريحان المشموم في هذا الموضع إنما هو قوت الناس

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī prefers the noncanonical nominative because it coordinates a full nominal clause with the preceding nominal clause; the common accusative attaches to يسجدان and implies a second verb, رفع السماء.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني الرفع هنا أظهر من قراءة الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa reading can be explained by deleting the preposition fī from “do not shortchange in the balance,” allowing the verb to take a direct object.
rows.anchor: فإنه على حذف حرف الجر أي لا تخسروا في الميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says they cannot leave without power God creates for them, including another place beyond heaven and earth; this shows God's control and power, proves His oneness, and warns them from disobedience.
rows.anchor: لا تخرجون إلا بقدرة من الله وقوة يعطيكموها بأن يخلق لكم مكانا آخر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the challenge to mean that people cannot learn what is in the heavens and earth without proof and explanation.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعلمونه إلا بحجة وبيان عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the phrase means that people cannot pass anywhere without witnessing God's proof of His oneness.
rows.anchor: لا تنفذون إلا بسلطان معناه حيث ما شاهدتم حجة الله وسلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessings include God's warning that they cannot escape, so they can prepare through obedience and avoiding sin, and His warning that passage requires proof so they can prepare for that day.
rows.anchor: أي بأي نعمه تكذبان أبإخباره عن تحيركم لتحتالوا له بعمل الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuwāẓ is the green flame that breaks away from a fire.
rows.anchor: وهو اللهب الأخضر المنقطع من النار

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس وسفيان وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid, Ibn ʿAbbās, Sufyān, and Qatāda identify nuḥās as molten copper for punishment.
rows.anchor: وهو الصفر المذاب للعذاب عن مجاهد وابن عباس وسفيان وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās in another transmission and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr take nuḥās to mean smoke.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النحاس الدخان عن ابن عباس في رواية أخرى وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify nuḥās as al-muhl.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النحاس المهل عن ابن مسعود والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the threat means that if people could escape, fire and molten metal would be sent upon them; another says this will be said to them on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه يقال لهم ذلك يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In a report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the heavens descend in sequence with their inhabitants until seven ranks of angels surround jinn and humans; a caller challenges them to pass, and they see seven rings of angels encircling them.
rows.anchor: روى مسعدة بن صدقة عن كليب قال كنا عند أبي عبد الله ع فأنشأ يحدثنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot repel the punishment from themselves or others; the verse shows they cannot escape recompense any more than they can pass beyond the horizons.
rows.anchor: أي فلا تقدران على دفع ذلك عنكما وعن غيركما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning itself is a great blessing because it deters people, while they can still choose, from committing evil.
rows.anchor: فإن وجه النعمة في إرسال الشواظ من النار والنحاس على الثقلين
